content_sections.heading: About KEA Textile Inspector
content_sections.text: The Karnataka Examinations Authority, a body of the Government of Karnataka, conducts this recruitment for the Handloom and Textiles Department. The posts belong to the Group-C cadre of the Kalyana-Karnataka region, and the appointing authority fills them on the basis of the competitive examination held by KEA. The notice states that post-wise and category-wise vacancy details given by the Handloom and Textiles Department will be published separately, that they are tentative, and that they may be revised according to Government orders issued from time to time.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: The qualification and certificate must be held on the last date fixed for applications. Candidates who have taken the examination and are awaiting results are not eligible. No qualification other than the one prescribed will be considered. Original marks cards and certificates must be produced at document verification; candidature is cancelled if they are not produced. If a candidate found ineligible takes part in the process, the candidature will be cancelled at any stage. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of the post. Under the Karnataka Civil Services (General Recruitment) Rules, 1977, candidates must have completed 18 years on the last date fixed for submission of applications. Government Order No. ಸಿಆಸುಇ 262 ಸೇನೆನಿ 2025 dated 29 January 2026 gives a one-time relaxation of 5 years in the upper age limit; after including it, candidates must not exceed the following: The candidate must be a citizen of India. A woman married to a man who already has a living wife is not eligible for appointment without prior permission of the Government. The candidate must be mentally and physically healthy and free from any physical defect likely to interfere with the duties. Persons permanently debarred by a Public Service Commission, KEA or any recruitment examination are not eligible. Persons convicted of moral turpitude, or temporarily debarred, are not eligible until the Government reviews the case and finds them fit.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The Textile Inspector post carries the pay scale of Rs. 54175-1375-58300-1500-64300-1650-74200-1900-85600-2300-99400. Candidates selected by direct recruitment will be on probation for two years. The National Pension System (NPS) applies to the post in the Handloom and Textiles Department.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Selection is through a competitive examination in Offline-OMR mode, with a compulsory Kannada Language Test for candidates who are not exempted. Paper-1 covers current events, everyday science, broad features of the Indian Constitution, history and geography of India with special reference to Karnataka, State and regional administration, development of Karnataka's economy including rural development, Panchayat Raj and rural cooperative institutions, and environmental issues and development of Karnataka. A minimum of 35% marks in the competitive examination is compulsory; candidates below it are not eligible for selection. Each question has 4 options; 0.25 mark is deducted for every wrong answer. A fifth option is given for unanswered questions, with five extra minutes after the last bell to shade it; 0.25 mark is deducted for any question with no option shaded. Candidates who studied Kannada as first or second language in the SSLC examination of the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board or an equivalent or higher examination, studied in Kannada medium, or passed a Kannada language test held by the Commission or another selection authority are exempted. For others, the test is an objective paper of 150 marks with a minimum of 50 marks to qualify, set to the standard of SSLC first-language Kannada. Absent candidates and those scoring below 50 are not eligible for selection. Its marks are not counted for merit. Centre details will be announced later. Admit cards are downloaded from the KEA website and must be carried with one original photo ID (PAN card, driving licence, Aadhaar card, passport, voter ID or Government employee ID). The examination centre cannot be changed for any reason.

faq.question: Q1. How many Textile Inspector vacancies are there in KEA Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are 5 Textile Inspector posts in the Kalyana-Karnataka Group-C cadre of the Handloom and Textiles Department; category-wise details will be published separately.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for KEA Textile Inspector?
faq.answer: The last date for the online application is 16 December 2026, and the fee can be paid until 17 December 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification is needed for Textile Inspector?
faq.answer: Candidates must hold a Diploma in Textiles or Handloom Technology or Diploma in Textiles Technology or Diploma in Handloom and Textile Technology on the last date of application.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit?
faq.answer: The minimum age is 18 years; the maximum is 40 years for General Merit, 43 years for Category 2A, 2B, 3A and 3B, and 45 years for SC/ST/Category-1, including the one-time 5-year relaxation.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary of a KEA Textile Inspector?
Q6. What is the application fee?
faq.answer: The fee is Rs. 750 for General Merit and Category 2A/2B/3A/3B, Rs. 500 for SC/ST/Category-1/Ex-servicemen/Third gender, and Rs. 250 for persons with disabilities, paid online and not refundable.

faq.question: Q7. How are Textile Inspectors selected?
faq.answer: Selection is through an Offline-OMR competitive examination of Paper-1 (General Knowledge) and Paper-2 (Specific Paper), each of 100 marks and 2 hours, with a minimum of 35% marks required.

faq.question: Q8. Is there negative marking in the KEA Textile Inspector exam?
faq.answer: Yes. 0.25 mark is deducted for each wrong answer, and also for each question where no option, including the fifth option, is shaded.

faq.question: Q9. When is the Kannada Language Test?
faq.answer: The Kannada Language Test is on 8 January 2027 from 3.00 PM to 5.00 PM; candidates need 50 out of 150 marks unless exempted.

faq.question: Q10. Is there a probation period?
faq.answer: Yes. Candidates selected by direct recruitment will be on probation for two years.
